w1_final.reason: The core fact is Samsung's Galaxy S28 launch announcement specifying 16GB base DRAM (up from 12GB predecessor) to enable on-device AI, plus a broader spring device-launch wave (Aurora Atlas Fold, Helio laptop, Pulseworks watch, etc.). None of the loaded events (E51, E73, E109, E107, E27) cover this product specification change or the multi-vendor AI-device launch cycle; they address memory-price pressure, Apple DRAM securing, and forward AI/robotics demand at a macro level.

candidates.proposition: Samsung announced the Galaxy S28 base model with 16GB of DRAM, one commercial configuration tier above the 12GB base capacity used in the preceding Galaxy S27 base model.
Samsung stated the Galaxy S28's 16GB base DRAM is aimed at supporting more on-device AI features, including longer context handling for translation, photo editing, and personal-search functions.
Samsung said the Galaxy S28 would be available for preorder in selected markets in the current month, with retail availability beginning later in the spring.

Aurora Mobile introduced the Atlas Fold, a folding handset with a lighter hinge, a larger exterior display, and a new method for shifting app windows between outer and inner screens; reservations opened in three countries with final pricing to be announced closer to availability.

Helio Systems showed a thin 14-inch laptop featuring a new neural-processing unit, a matte low-power display, a magnetic accessory rail, and an offline transcription application, arriving in two processor options.
Pulseworks unveiled a fitness watch with a more precise skin-temperature sensor and a redesigned charging puck, capable of flagging changes in recovery patterns but not intended to diagnose illness.
Luma Health introduced a sleep ring adding a daytime stress score based on movement and heart-rate variability.

Northline introduced a countertop display combining recipe suggestions with a family calendar; Atria Robotics demonstrated a compact floor cleaner that maps rooms without relying continuously on a cloud connection.
Samsung did not identify component suppliers or disclose supplier shares in its Galaxy S28 launch material.
